nora: Weird bug on Pixel 8 emulator with kotlin-sdk + retrofit: rapid duplicate POSTs when token refresh happens during streaming requests.
kevin: streaming POST as in non-repeatable RequestBody?
nora: yes. We stream a JSON NDJSON body from an InputStream. If a 401 triggers a refresh mid-upload some chunks get replayed and server sees duplicate records.
jin: do you have the RequestBody impl?
nora: tiny snippet:
```kotlin
class NdjsonBody(val input: InputStream): RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/x-ndjson".toMediaType()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) { input.source().use { it.readAll(sink) } }
}
```
kevin: OkHttp can retry or re-open streams when an Authenticator/Interceptor flow blocks the dispatcher. If the body isn't repeatable you'll get duplicates.
nora: quick fixes that worked: 1) make body repeatable (buffer to temp file) 2) disable retryOnConnectionFailure for the upload client 3) run auth refresh on a separate OkHttpClient so dispatcher isn't blocked.
ops-bot: CI run 4412 started for repro branch streaming-dup-check: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/4412
kevin: doc ask: add a short devex note about "Non-repeatable bodies + auth refresh -> duplicate side-effects" and include code snippets for dedicated auth client + disabling retry. I'll open the PR.
nora: added a minimal emulator test that toggles retryOnConnectionFailure and reproduces the duplicate with 6 concurrent uploads. Will attach to the PR.
